title: SRE dashboards + alerting for tiered batching SLOs (fast/standard/cost-efficient)
creator: Sean Gallagher
project: Cost Optimization Automation: Workload-aware batching defaults
description:
Goal
- Provide SRE + oncall-ready dashboards and alerting to monitor tiered batching behavior and enforce latency SLOs per tier (fast / standard / cost-efficient).
- Support staged rollout monitoring (feature flag ramps by model/region) with clear abort conditions and owner assignments.

Context
- Runtime work introduces batching_tier and workload-aware parameter mapping (queue delay, batch formation) behind a flag.
- We need consistent per-tier attribution so we can compare performance and avoid noisy alerts during ramp.

Primary users
- Runtime oncall (serving-runtime)
- SRE oncall (inference platform)
- Product (Optimize) + Solutions Engineering during beta cohort validation

Links
- Confluence SLO tier definitions: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient.json
- Confluence dashboards/alerts spec (target): sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tiered-batching-observability-dashboards.json
- Metrics implementation ticket: ENG-18422
- Perf canary coverage: ENG-18423
- Observability pack PR (dashboards JSON): sources/github/observability-pack/pr_289.json
- SLO toolkit helpers (tier labels + error budgets): sources/github/slo-toolkit/pr_267.json

Scope
1) Dashboards (Grafana + Console-friendly JSON definitions)
- Tier overview landing dashboard:
  - p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency (by route: chat/completions/embeddings; by model; by region)
  - queue delay distribution (p50/p95/p99) + batch wait time
  - batch size distribution (prefill + decode) and batch formation rate
  - throughput (tokens/s) and effective cost signals ($/1M tokens proxy where available)
  - GPU utilization + memory pressure/KV cache pressure (if exported)
  - timeouts/cancellations + load-shed reason codes
  - breakdown by batching_tier label and by “effective tier” (see note below)

- Rollout dashboard (ramp monitoring):
  - time series of flag exposure (% requests tiered defaults enabled) by model+region
  - compare control vs treatment (tiered enabled vs disabled) for p95 latency and errors
  - canary cohort filters (beta accounts / dedicated pools)

- Debug dashboard (tail latency):
  - stage timings: prefill latency, decode latency, scheduler queue delay
  - top contributors: prompt length buckets, concurrency buckets, streaming vs non-streaming
  - linkouts to traces for high queue delay / high p99 slices

2) Alerting rules (per tier, with noise controls)
- Latency SLO burn alerts (multi-window, multi-burn) per tier:
  - fast tier: aggressive paging thresholds
  - standard tier: paging for sustained burn; ticket for slower burn
  - cost-efficient tier: paging primarily for error spikes / severe regressions; latency burn goes to ticket unless extreme (still must not violate contractual SLO if sold)

- Queue delay guardrail alerts:
  - alert on sustained elevated queue delay p95 AND increasing timeout/cancel rate
  - do not page on queue delay alone unless correlated with latency SLO burn

- Error-rate alerts:
  - 5xx rate, timeout rate, cancellation rate (client-aborted vs server-canceled), overload/load-shed rate
  - separate alert routes for “expected” load-shed (cost-efficient under overload) vs unexpected (fast tier shedding)

- Saturation alerts:
  - GPU util pinned with rising queue delay
  - KV cache pressure / OOM near-miss counters (if available) leading indicators for cost-efficient tier regressions

3) Attribution + labeling requirements
- Ensure dashboards/alerts use stable labels:
  - batching_tier (requested tier)
  - effective_batching_tier (resolved tier after precedence/overrides)
  - model, model_family, region, route, deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private)
  - streaming (true/false)
- NOTE: Until “effective config explain” endpoint is fully deployed, we’ll treat effective_batching_tier as best-effort from runtime labels. Once PR_18470 lands broadly, align dashboard to display “requested vs effective” side-by-side.

Deliverables
- Merged dashboard JSON and alerts into observability-pack (PR_289) with documentation for importing into Grafana and for Console embedding.
- Alert definitions checked into monitoring repo (or observability-pack, depending on current ownership), with routing to #oncall-inference-runtime and pager policy confirmed with Rafael.
- Rollout monitoring checklist (below) posted to #eng-sre and linked from release brief.

Acceptance criteria
- A new oncall can answer, within 5 minutes:
  1) Are fast/standard/cost-efficient meeting p95/p99 targets for the beta models/regions?
  2) If not, is the driver queue delay, prefill, decode, or downstream (model/backends)?
  3) Is the regression limited to streaming vs non-streaming, prompt length buckets, or concurrency buckets?
  4) What changed recently (flag ramp, runtime release, model registry defaults update)?

- Alerts:
  - Latency burn alerts page correctly during a controlled “bad rollout” test in staging.
  - Queue-delay-only spikes do not page during low traffic / known batch formation jitter.
  - Alert labels include batching tier and model/region for actionable triage.

Open questions / risks
- Queue delay metrics can be noisy at low QPS; we must enforce minimum traffic / sample thresholds in alert queries.
- Cost-efficient tier is allowed higher queueing; avoid false positives by using tier-specific thresholds and correlating with timeouts and SLO burn.

Rollout monitoring checklist (for beta ramps)
Pre-ramp (T-24h)
- [ ] Confirm dashboards show tier breakdown in staging for at least 1 hour of load.
- [ ] Confirm alert rules deployed but muted in staging; run synthetic regression to validate firing.
- [ ] Confirm ownership: Runtime oncall (primary) + SRE oncall (secondary) + Product DRI informed.
- [ ] Confirm abort criteria pasted into rollout thread.

During ramp
- Watch (every 15 minutes for first hour, then hourly):
  - p95/p99 latency per tier, per model+region
  - queue delay p95 and batch wait time; batch size distribution shifts
  - timeout/cancel + 5xx; overload/load-shed reason codes
  - GPU util pinned / memory pressure
- Abort / rollback signals (any tier):
  - sustained p95 regression > threshold for 2 consecutive windows OR p99 spike correlated with queue delay
  - timeout rate +0.3% absolute sustained for 10 minutes on any high-traffic model/region
  - fast tier: ANY load-shed events above baseline (unless explicitly enabled for incident mitigation)

Post-ramp (T+24h)
- [ ] Write a short summary in rollout thread with screenshots/links (before/after).
- [ ] File follow-ups for noisy panels/alerts and any missing slices (prompt buckets, streaming cadence).
- [ ] Confirm dashboards pinned in Console (if applicable) and linked from beta release notes.
